METHODS FOK THERMAL SHOCK TESTS ON GLASSWARE
0. FOREW~ORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Jndian Standards Institution on 2 February 1972, after the draft finalized by the Glassware Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 The term ` thermal shock ' is used to refer to the strain produced when a temperature difference is suddenly created between the inner and outer walls of a container. Such temperature differences occur in various ways Assrssmcnt of the abiti ty of a g!ass container to withstand in practice. thcrmnl shock is, therefore, essential to c`nsurka satisfactory service. ~0.3 For test purposes the most direct and severe way of producing thermal shock is to heat the article by placing it in a hot air-oven or by immersing it in a hot water-bath at a known temperature and then transferring it to a` cold water-bath or spraying cold water on it, thus However, to obtain reproducible results it is chilling the outside surface, essential that factors such as period of keeping the article in hot airoven or its immersion in hot water-bath, time of transfer and method and keeping it uniform are standardized. of controlling temperature Further, keeping in view the end use of the article and the severity of thermal shock rcquircd, four methods of test have been prescribed in this standard. 0.4 In the formulation of this standard due lveightage has been given to international coordination among the standards and practices prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the field in this country. This has been met by basing the standard on ISO/R 718 ` Methods for thermal shock tests on laboratory glassware ' issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ). 0.4.1 Assistance has. also been rendered by the Central Glass and Ceramic Research Institute, Calcutta in the development and finalization of the method applicable to flat jvare. 0.5 This standard is one of the series of Indian Standards on testing the quality of glassware. Othc~r standards published so far in the series are: IS : 2303-1963 Method of grading glass for alkalinity IS: 5633-1970 Method for determination of cnpfiicirnt thermal expansion of glass 3 of` Iillcn

5.3.2 Finally examine the rims for any damage or cracks.

5.4 Method D-Neat the air-oven and adjust the temperature to t, 5 l"C, taking for convenience the temperature of tap water to be sprayed as I,, and selecting fI to give the required thermal shock ( t, - tz)`C. Plack the articles in the air-oven and maintain for 30 minutes. 5.4.1 Then remove the articles from the air-oven, one at a time, by means the process of transference J tongs with asbestos-covered tips, completing 1L1j f 1 seconds for each article,. and spray tap water from the sprayer on the convex side of the article for a specified period which shall not exceed one minute, without allowing the concave side of the article to become wet. The spraying shall be done at a pressure of 1 kgf/cmz keeping the surface to be sprayed at a distance of about 30 cm from the sprayer. 5.4.2 Finally examine the articles for any damage or cracks.
